title: The Ninth Child: from Headington Hill to a Camp in Texas
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Maisons-Laffitte, the ninth child born on Christmas Day
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin corrected from a gathering-pass figure 1.1 km off
stops.campa: In a suburb west of Paris, on Christmas Day, the ninth and youngest child of Robert Maxwell is born and given three names: Ghislaine, Noelle, Marion. Her father was born Jan Ludvik Hoch in Slatinske Doly, in Czechoslovakia, and is by now a British publisher and a Member of Parliament. Two days after she is born her brother Michael is injured in a car crash and does not wake from it. He lives another seven years in the coma. The household she is born into spends those seven years arranged around that bed.
suggested_refs: Maisons-Laffitte, Yvelines, the Paris suburb where the Maxwells were briefly resident in 1961

stops.name: Headington Hill Hall, the mansion rented from the council
stops.date_confidence: year attested for Michael's death; month defaulted
stops.campa: Michael dies this year, after seven years in the coma. The house is fifty-three rooms rented from Oxford City Council, with the offices of Pergamon Press on the ground floor: her father's scientific journals are printed and sold out of the building his family lives in. Robert Maxwell holds the lease for the last thirty-two years of his life. She is the last of his nine children, born when the publisher was already made, and the one he is said to favour. She is six when her brother is buried.
suggested_refs: Headington Hill Hall, Headington Road, Oxford OX3 0BF, headquarters of Pergamon Press

stops.name: Edgarley Hall, sent away at nine
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; press biographies only, school records not public, month defaulted
stops.campa: At about nine she is sent west into Somerset, to the preparatory school under Glastonbury Tor that feeds Millfield. The dating rests on press reconstruction: no school record is public, and the atlas carries this stop as unproven. From this year she is educated away from Headington. She boards; she is collected at the ends of terms and returned at the beginnings of them; and the house on the hill becomes an address she visits between school years.
suggested_refs: Edgarley Hall, the Millfield preparatory school near Glastonbury
sources: Guardian and Vanity Fair biographical profiles

stops.name: Headington School, the return to Oxford
stops.date_confidence: attested as 'from age thirteen'; month defaulted
stops.campa: At about thirteen she comes back to Oxford, to the girls' school a mile east of her father's mansion, near enough to see the Hall from the road. Her brothers and sisters are already dispersed into the Maxwell companies and the Maxwell marriages. She is the youngest of nine in a family whose name is going onto a printing house, a football club, and before the decade ends a fleet of newspapers. Oxford High School for Girls had her before this; Headington keeps her until the sixth form.
suggested_refs: Headington School, Oxford, attended from about 1974

stops.name: Marlborough College, the last school
stops.date_confidence: traditional; sources give only 'late 1970s', pin corrected by about 1 km
stops.campa: For A-Levels she is sent into Wiltshire, to a school that opened its sixth form to girls in 1968 and still admits very few of them. The year of her arrival is approximate; the sources give only the late nineteen-seventies, and the atlas prints 1980 as a placement. She is being pointed at Oxford and at the drawing rooms beyond Oxford. Marlborough is the last school. What follows is Balliol, and after Balliol there is no more schooling, only the business of being a Maxwell.
suggested_refs: Marlborough College, Wiltshire, which opened its sixth form to girls in 1968

stops.name: Balliol College, the degree in Modern History
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month inferred from the Oxford graduation calendar
stops.campa: She takes a degree in Modern History with Languages from one of the oldest colleges in Oxford, half a mile from the mansion where she was raised. It is the only qualification she will ever hold in her own name. Her father, driven out of a Czech village school by war before he was fifteen, has put his youngest through the institution that certifies the English governing class. She leaves it with the accent and the address book, and both of them work for the next thirty years.
suggested_refs: Balliol College, Oxford, matriculation and degree records, 1982-1985

stops.name: Belgravia, the yacht that carries her name
stops.date_confidence: year attested for the naming; the London social life is dated only to 'the late 1980s'
stops.campa: Her father names his yacht the Lady Ghislaine, and she becomes a fixture of the London season: a women's club founded on the model of the old Kit-Cat, the society pages, the Belgravia addresses. She is being used, and consents to be used, as the presentable face of a proprietor whom Fleet Street distrusts. Five years from now the yacht will be the last place her father is seen alive, and the name on its stern will be printed in every newspaper on earth beside a photograph of her.
suggested_refs: The motor yacht Lady Ghislaine, named 1986
sources: Tatler and Vanity Fair profiles cited via Wikipedia

stops.name: John F. Kennedy International Airport, the envelope
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from press timelines; no primary document, month as given, day defaulted
stops.campa: She flies the Atlantic carrying an envelope for her father, an errand no document survives to prove; the atlas records it as press reconstruction and nothing firmer. In January he agrees to buy the New York Daily News and in March he takes control of it, and she is posted to Manhattan as his emissary in the city. A widely repeated account has the two of them crossing together by Concorde that May. Verification does not support it, and the crossing is left standing as a story rather than a fact.
suggested_refs: Robert Maxwell's acquisition of the New York Daily News, January to March 1991

stops.name: Puerto de La Luz, the body brought ashore
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The Lady Ghislaine is at sea off the Canaries with one passenger, and in the night that passenger goes over the side. The body is recovered from the Atlantic and brought ashore at Las Palmas. Spanish pathologists and a British inquest do not agree on what killed him, and his daughter rejects both accident and suicide. Within days the pension funds of Mirror Group are found empty. Reporting outside this atlas ties his financing to the BCCI network that clark_clifford and adnan_khashoggi travel through here; no journey file states the link, and it stands as adjacency, not contact.
suggested_refs: Puerto de La Luz, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, where Robert Maxwell's body was landed, 5 November 1991

stops.name: Mount of Olives, the state funeral
stops.date_confidence: date attested; the pool gives two coordinates 400 m apart along the ridge and the atlas does not settle which
stops.campa: He is buried on the ridge facing the old city, in a state funeral the Israeli government arranges: Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir attends, President Chaim Herzog attends, and the eulogies speak of a Czech Jewish boy who lost his family to the camps and came back a press baron. His youngest daughter stands at the graveside, five days a mourner and already an heiress to a hole. Two lenses of the record place this grave four hundred metres apart, and the atlas prints the disagreement instead of choosing.
suggested_refs: The Mount of Olives Jewish cemetery, Jerusalem, burial of 10 November 1991

stops.name: Central Park West, the borrowed apartment
stops.date_confidence: year attested; exact building never publicly confirmed, so the pin is approximate and the month defaulted
stops.campa: She takes an apartment overlooking Central Park, lent by an Iranian friend, and a job at a real estate office on Madison Avenue, and lives on roughly eighty thousand pounds a year from a trust her father could not reach. No public record gives the building, so the pin is an approximation and is marked as one. She is thirty, the daughter of a bankrupt fraud, in a city where her surname has become a headline about missing money. By February of the following year she is documented at Jeffrey Epstein's side.
suggested_refs: The Madison Avenue real estate office and the borrowed Central Park apartment of 1992, neither address confirmed

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the Straus house
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1993; day defaulted
stops.campa: The Herbert N. Straus House on the Upper East Side is the largest private residence in Manhattan. Epstein holds it from Leslie Wexner. From early 1993 she is documented there, and for a decade she is the house: who is invited, who is hired, who is driven to it and away from it. Prosecutors will allege the two were lovers in these years; she says the physical relationship ended in 2001; Epstein's pilot dates her withdrawal to 2004. The atlas records all three datings and reconciles none of them.
suggested_refs: The Herbert N. Straus House, 9 East 71st Street, Manhattan
sources: US v. Maxwell trial record, SDNY 2021

stops.name: 358 El Brillo Way, the Palm Beach house
stops.date_confidence: the house's role is attested at trial; this year is a placement within a 1990s-2005 window, month defaulted, pin corrected 2.5 km
stops.campa: The Palm Beach house is low, pink, and unremarkable from the street. Trial testimony a quarter of a century later describes girls brought to this address for massages that were not massages, recruited and directed by her. Palm Beach police open a file on the house in 2005. The year on this stop is a placement inside a long window, not a record. A suit filed in 2020 separately alleges she recruited a thirteen-year-old at a Michigan arts academy in July 1994, an allegation no court has tried.
suggested_refs: 358 El Brillo Way, Palm Beach, and the 2005 Palm Beach Police investigation file
sources: US v. Maxwell trial testimony, SDNY, November-December 2021

stops.name: Zorro Ranch, the New Mexico holding
stops.date_confidence: the ranch's role is attested; this year is a placement, month defaulted, pin corrected 14 km
stops.campa: Seven thousand six hundred acres owned outright below the Ortiz Mountains, called ten thousand by every account that folds in the leased state land beside it. Accusers and witnesses name it as a place she visited and a place where trafficking happened. In the same year Maria Farmer alleges that she and Epstein assaulted her; Farmer swears the affidavit in April 2019, twenty-three years afterwards, and no court ever tries the claim. The record gives no location for that assault, so it is stated here and left unpinned.
suggested_refs: Zorro Ranch, near Stanley, New Mexico; the 2019 New Mexico Attorney General civil suit
sources: US v. Maxwell trial record and victim testimony, SDNY 2021

stops.name: Belgravia, the London house kept in parallel
stops.date_confidence: attested as 'from 1997 onward'; month defaulted
stops.campa: From this year she keeps a house in Belgravia, and the London life runs in parallel with the New York one for a decade. The year before, she was arrested for drink-driving in west London, and the papers gave her occupation as internet operator. The atlas assigns that arrest no pin, because west London is not a place and the Belgravia address is not the same address. She is by now two women in two cities, and the passage between them is the working part of the arrangement.
suggested_refs: The Belgravia townhouse, held from 1997

stops.name: Little Saint James, the island
stops.date_confidence: the island's role is attested across 1998-2019; this year opens the window, month defaulted
stops.campa: Seventy acres of scrub and cut stone in the US Virgin Islands, bought and rebuilt across two decades. Witnesses testify that she flew the helicopter carrying guests in from St Thomas, and that she recruited and directed the girls brought out to the island. The geography is the case: a place reached only by boat or by air, one host, one pilot, where arriving and leaving are both permissions granted by somebody else. In May 2023 it is sold with its undeveloped neighbour for sixty million dollars.
suggested_refs: Little Saint James, US Virgin Islands; FBI search warrant affidavits, 2019
sources: US v. Maxwell trial testimony, SDNY 2021

stops.name: Avenue Foch, the Paris apartment
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; press investigations place her in charge of the apartment across the 1990s and 2000s, exact unit and date unconfirmed
stops.campa: An apartment on the widest avenue in Paris, twelve miles from the suburb where she was born, held by Epstein and managed by her. The Miami Herald and others place her in charge of it; the precise door is on no public record, and the stop is carried as reconstruction. It is one node of a property network that investigators will map twenty years later: New York, Palm Beach, New Mexico, the islands, Paris. She moves along it as a resident of all of them and the registered owner of none.
suggested_refs: The Avenue Foch apartment, Paris, examined in the Miami Herald 'Perversion of Justice' series

stops.name: Necker Island, the March stay
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; her presence on this specific stay is disputed and unconfirmed, pin corrected 3.7 km
stops.campa: A stay on Richard Branson's island in March, in the same company as Prince Andrew and Epstein, reported in the press and cited in later civil filings, and mentioned nowhere in the standard account of Virginia Giuffre's life. The atlas carries it as reconstruction and says so on the face of the stop. The reporting gives the month, and no filing gives a day. Four months later she walks into the spa at Mar-a-Lago and offers a sixteen-year-old a job.
suggested_refs: Necker Island, British Virgin Islands, and the reported March 2000 gathering

stops.name: Mar-a-Lago, the spa attendant
stops.date_confidence: mid-2000 attested; month approximate, day defaulted, pin corrected 3.1 km
stops.campa: At the Palm Beach club she approaches a sixteen-year-old spa attendant and offers her work as a travelling masseuse for a wealthy man. The girl is Virginia Roberts, born in August 1983. Prosecutors and her civil complaint agree on this scene. The gathering pass dated it a year late, and the atlas moves it back to mid-2000, because 2001 is the year of the photograph and not the year of the recruitment. The month here is approximate. Everything that follows from this conversation is litigation.
suggested_refs: Mar-a-Lago, Palm Beach, and the spa where Giuffre was working in 2000
sources: US v. Maxwell trial record, SDNY 2021

stops.name: 116 East 65th Street, the townhouse six blocks away
stops.date_confidence: year attested from property records; month and day inferred
stops.campa: Seven thousand square feet, six blocks from Epstein's mansion, taken through an anonymous limited liability company registered to the same address as one of his own companies. Property records surface it nineteen years afterwards. She now has Belgravia, the Upper East Side, and the run of four other houses she does not own. Her name is on none of the deeds and on none of the company filings; what ties her to this townhouse is the address the paperwork shares with him.
suggested_refs: 116 East 65th Street, Manhattan, and the LLC filings that surfaced it in 2019
sources: New York Times and Daily Beast property investigations, 2019-2021

stops.name: Sandringham House, the thirty-ninth birthday
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the pool's 'November' is impossible against a 25 December birth, so December is inferred and flagged; pin corrected 700 m
stops.campa: Epstein attends a party at the royal estate in Norfolk, said to be held for her thirty-ninth birthday. She was born on Christmas Day 1961, so a thirty-ninth birthday falls in December 2000; the sources say only that it happened that year, and the month here is inference rather than record. The financier comes through the door on her introduction. She is thirty-nine that month and he is forty-seven. Eight years from now he will plead guilty in a Florida court to soliciting a minor for prostitution.
suggested_refs: Sandringham House, Norfolk, and the 2000 party attended by Epstein
sources: UK press reporting cited via Wikipedia, 'Ghislaine Maxwell'

stops.name: Belgravia, the photograph in the hallway
stops.date_confidence: attested to March 2001; day defaulted
stops.campa: In her London townhouse a photograph is taken: Prince Andrew with his arm around the waist of a seventeen-year-old, and behind them, in the doorway, smiling, she stands. The Mail on Sunday publishes it ten years later and it is authenticated in civil filings ten years after that. The image shows three people in a hallway and nothing else. The age of the girl in it is the fact the litigation turns on. The house is hers. So is the introduction that put them in it.
suggested_refs: The March 2001 Belgravia photograph, published by the Mail on Sunday in 2011

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the Vanity Fair profile
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month inferred
stops.campa: Vicky Ward profiles Epstein for Vanity Fair and records what he calls the woman who runs his houses. In the same year she is linked to Ted Waitt, founder of Gateway Computers, in a relationship reported to run until 2010. Two lives are being kept at once and both of them are on the record. Her withdrawal from Epstein's orbit begins here, or in 2001 by her own later account, or in 2004 by his pilot's, and no source reconciles the three datings with each other.
stops.quote_source: Jeffrey Epstein on Ghislaine Maxwell, in Vicky Ward's Vanity Fair profile, 2003, cited via Wikipedia, 'Ghislaine Maxwell'
suggested_refs: Vicky Ward's 2003 Vanity Fair profile of Jeffrey Epstein
sources: Vicky Ward, Vanity Fair, 2003, cited via Wikipedia

stops.name: Manchester-by-the-Sea, the house on the shore
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month defaulted; the pool's competing 2016 start date is the marriage year, not the move
stops.campa: She begins living with Scott Borgerson, an entrepreneur and Arctic shipping analyst, on the Massachusetts coast north of Boston. The gathering pass dated the move to 2016 and the atlas corrects it: 2016 is the year they marry in secret, not the year she arrives. For twelve years the town sees a woman who sails and keeps to herself. The other half of her life is in Florida, where a state investigation into the Palm Beach house is a year old and closing on the man who owns it.
suggested_refs: The Borgerson house at Manchester-by-the-Sea, Massachusetts
sources: Daily Mail and New York Times location investigations, 2019-2020

stops.name: 358 El Brillo Way, the Florida plea
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the day is the conventional date of the state plea and is inferred
stops.campa: Epstein pleads to soliciting a minor for prostitution in a Florida state court and serves thirteen months, much of it on work release. The federal non-prosecution agreement signed the year before is the instrument that closes the investigation. She is not charged. Sixteen years from now the Second Circuit will hold that this agreement never barred her prosecution. Until that ruling, the thirteen months on work release stand as the whole of the punishment the case has produced.
suggested_refs: The 2007 federal non-prosecution agreement and the 2008 Florida state plea

stops.name: United Nations Headquarters, the TerraMar Project
stops.date_confidence: founding year attested; month inferred
stops.campa: She founds the TerraMar Project, an ocean-conservation nonprofit, and carries it into United Nations events for seven years. In 2014 she speaks at TEDx Charlottesville about the sea; no verified coordinate for that stage exists in the record, so it is said here and not pinned. For most of this decade the philanthropy is the entire public answer to the question of what she does, and the answer is given in rooms full of ambassadors, forty blocks from the house on East 71st Street.
suggested_refs: The TerraMar Project's public filings and its UN-affiliated appearances, 2012-2019

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the defamation complaint
stops.date_confidence: month attested; day defaulted; the pool gives this courthouse at two coordinates 60 m apart
stops.campa: Virginia Roberts Giuffre sues her for defamation in the Southern District of New York. The claim is narrow: that in calling Giuffre a liar she defamed her. The consequence is not narrow. Discovery in this civil case produces the deposition, the exhibits, and the unsealing fights that run for five years and put on a public docket what no criminal process had yet touched. In January of this year, filings in a related case had already described the grooming, in a deposition attributed to Giuffre as Jane Doe 3.
suggested_refs: Giuffre v. Maxwell, No. 1:15-cv-07433-LAP (S.D.N.Y.), filed September 2015

stops.name: Manchester-by-the-Sea, the marriage nobody is told about
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day unknown and defaulted
stops.campa: She marries Scott Borgerson. Nobody is told. The marriage stays off the public record for four years and surfaces only when federal prosecutors argue against bail and her lawyers are obliged to name a husband. The month here is unknown and defaulted to January. She is fifty-four, living on the Massachusetts shore under a name that nobody in the town connects to the Mirror Group or to the Upper East Side, and the civil case in Manhattan is a few months from putting her under oath.
suggested_refs: The 2016 Maxwell-Borgerson marriage, unreported until 2020
sources: US v. Maxwell bail filings, SDNY 2020

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the deposition entered on the docket
stops.date_confidence: attested; the deposition was taken at the offices of Boies Schiller and Flexner and is pinned to the docket that holds it, not to the room
stops.campa: She is deposed for the defamation case docketed at this courthouse, in a law firm's conference room across town. The transcript runs four hundred and sixty-five pages. In it the phrase I don't recall appears seventy-six times, seven of them as the whole of the answer. The document reaches the public docket on 22 October 2020, not in the August release it is usually credited to. What she does not recall, on the page, is what she was paid and by whom, in the years when she was running the houses.
stops.quote: Q. In 1992 I know you gave me the description of the work that you were performing for him, how much was he paying you, do you remember? A. I don't recall. Q. Do you know for example in 2001 how much he was paying you? A. I don't recall.
stops.quote_source: Deposition of Ghislaine Maxwell, Giuffre v. Maxwell, No. 1:15-cv-07433-LAP (S.D.N.Y.), 22 April 2016, transcript pp. 101-102; filed as Dkt. 1137-13 (Exhibit 6), 22 October 2020
suggested_refs: Giuffre v. Maxwell, Dkt. 1137-13 (Exhibit 6), the 465-page deposition transcript of 22 April 2016
sources: Filed transcript, Giuffre v. Maxwell, Dkt. 1137-13
SDNY docket (CourtListener returned HTTP 403 on every attempt)

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, settled under seal
stops.date_confidence: month attested; the gathering pass had May and is corrected; day defaulted
stops.campa: The defamation case settles under seal for a sum reported in the millions. The gathering pass put this in May and the record puts it in June. Sealing is the whole point of the settlement, and it holds for two and a half years, until a judge in this building begins releasing the file in batches. Everything the criminal case will later use has by now been said once, on paper, in a civil suit that was formally about whether one woman had called another woman a liar.
suggested_refs: The sealed June 2017 settlement in Giuffre v. Maxwell

segments.name: August 2019 and the House at Bradford

stops.name: In-N-Out Burger, Los Angeles, the photograph that proves she is there
stops.date_confidence: month attested; day inferred; the specific branch has never been identified and the pin is approximate
stops.campa: Epstein dies in a Manhattan federal jail in August, ruled a suicide by the authorities, and the only question left in the press is where she is. Days later the New York Post prints a photograph of her at a Los Angeles hamburger counter with a dog and a book. The image is read as an answer: she has not left the country. No reporting has ever identified the branch and the pin is approximate. It is the last picture of her at liberty that the public is given.
suggested_refs: The New York Post photograph of August 2019, location never independently confirmed

stops.name: Bradford, New Hampshire, the hundred and fifty-six acres
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month inferred; this pin was not offered a correction in verification and is carried as received
stops.campa: She acquires a hundred and fifty-six acre property in a New Hampshire town of some sixteen hundred people, and stops appearing anywhere. Prosecutors will say afterwards that she moved houses, changed her phone, and had deliveries made under another name. The month here is inference. For half a year, while a federal grand jury sits in Manhattan, the woman who ran six houses on two continents lives on a wooded lot with no near neighbour and does not come out of it.
suggested_refs: The Bradford, New Hampshire property, purchased through an entity in 2019

stops.name: Bradford, New Hampshire, the arrest
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: FBI agents come up the drive in the morning, find the gate locked, and go through it. She is located inside by a device that reads the signal of a mobile phone. Six federal counts are unsealed the same day, among them conspiracy to commit sex trafficking. Twenty-nine years after her father put her on a plane to New York to be his emissary, the government of the United States has the daughter, and for the first time in this case the defendant is a living person who can be tried.
suggested_refs: DOJ press release announcing the arrest, 2 July 2020

stops.name: Metropolitan Detention Center, Brooklyn, bail refused
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin corrected 3.9 km from a figure landing in Gowanus
stops.campa: She pleads not guilty at arraignment and is refused bail as a flight risk. She is held in the federal jail at Sunset Park for two years, through the superseding indictment of March 2021 that adds a count of sex trafficking a fourteen-year-old between 2001 and 2004, and her lawyers protest the conditions repeatedly and without effect. The gathering pass placed this jail four kilometres away in Gowanus; the atlas moves the pin onto the building that actually holds her.
suggested_refs: Metropolitan Detention Center, 80 29th Street, Brooklyn, NY 11232
sources: US v. Maxwell court filings, SDNY 2020-2022

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the trial opens
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Opening statements in United States versus Ghislaine Maxwell. Across four weeks four women testify, three of them under pseudonyms, describing recruitment as teenagers and describing her as the one who did it: who found them and who was in the room. The defence argues that she is standing in for a dead man. The government argues that a dead man cannot recruit anybody. The courthouse appears in the record at two coordinates sixty metres apart, and the atlas notes the split without resolving it.
suggested_refs: US v. Ghislaine Maxwell, SDNY, trial transcript, November-December 2021

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the verdict
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The jury convicts on five counts of six, including sex trafficking of a minor, and acquits on the count of enticing a minor to travel to engage in illegal sex acts. Sixty years and four days after she was born in a French suburb on Christmas Day, the youngest of Robert Maxwell's nine children is a convicted federal felon. It is the first judicial finding of fact about anything that happened inside the houses, and it is made by twelve people who had never heard of any of them.
suggested_refs: The jury verdict of 29 December 2021, SDNY

stops.name: 500 Pearl Street, the sentence
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Judge Alison Nathan imposes twenty years, two hundred and forty months, with a fine and supervised release to follow. It closes a proceeding that began as a civil defamation suit in 2015 and became, by way of a dead defendant, the only criminal accounting anyone in this network has faced. She is sixty. The Bureau of Prisons publishes a release date of 17 July 2037. Two years from now the Court of Appeals will affirm the sentence without shortening it by a day.
suggested_refs: The sentencing record, US v. Maxwell, 28 June 2022

stops.name: FCI Tallahassee, the transfer south
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin corrected 5.3 km from a figure pointing at downtown Tallahassee
stops.campa: Four weeks after sentencing she is moved from Brooklyn to a low-security women's prison in the Florida panhandle, four hundred miles up the coast from Palm Beach. The gathering pass placed the facility downtown, five kilometres west of where it stands on Capital Circle, and the atlas corrects the pin. Press reporting says she converts to Judaism here, around 2023, which is the faith her father was buried in on the Mount of Olives. The conversion is reported and it is not confirmed.
suggested_refs: Federal Correctional Institution, Tallahassee, 501 Capital Circle N.E.

stops.name: Thurgood Marshall Courthouse, the appeal refused
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool gives this courthouse 60 m from the district court pin and the atlas keeps both as given
stops.campa: The Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit affirms conviction and sentence. Her central argument was that the non-prosecution agreement Epstein signed with federal prosecutors in Florida in 2007 covered her as well, and barred the government from charging her seventeen years later in New York. The court holds that it did not. The agreement that closed the first investigation, and that has shadowed every investigation since, is read once in public and found not to reach her.
suggested_refs: Second Circuit opinion affirming the conviction, September 2024

stops.name: FCI Tallahassee, two days with the Deputy Attorney General
stops.date_confidence: attested as a two-day interview beginning 24 July 2025
stops.campa: Todd Blanche, Deputy Attorney General of the United States, comes to the prison and interviews her across two days. The Department is under sustained congressional and public pressure over its handling of the Epstein files. Epstein has been dead six years; she is the person still living who was inside the houses with him. What she said is not published in full. Eight days later she is moved from this low-security prison in the Florida panhandle to a minimum-security camp in Texas.
suggested_refs: The July 2025 Department of Justice interviews at FCI Tallahassee

stops.name: Federal Prison Camp Bryan, the camp in Texas
stops.date_confidence: attested; pin corrected 1.1 km from the Bryan town centre
stops.campa: She is transferred to a minimum-security federal prison camp in central Texas: no perimeter fence, dormitory housing, work assignments. Eight days after two days of interviews with the Deputy Attorney General. Critics call the move payment and the Bureau of Prisons calls it classification. The atlas records the two dates in order and the dispute as a dispute, and does not decide it. The gathering pass put this camp at the Bryan town centre, a kilometre from the gate on Ursuline Avenue.
suggested_refs: Federal Prison Camp Bryan, 1100 Ursuline Avenue, Bryan, Texas 77803

stops.name: Supreme Court of the United States, certiorari denied
stops.date_confidence: date attested; no coordinate for the building appears in the verified pool and this pin is supplied from general knowledge
stops.campa: The Supreme Court declines to hear her appeal, without comment, in a list of denials. The conviction is final. No coordinate for the building on First Street appears in the verified record for this life, and the pin here is supplied from general knowledge, which the atlas states rather than conceals. Ten weeks earlier the Deputy Attorney General had sat with her for two days; the denial arrives while a pardon is being discussed openly in Washington, and it does not touch that question at all.
suggested_refs: The order list of 6 October 2025 denying certiorari

stops.name: Federal Prison Camp Bryan, the Fifth Amendment
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: She is deposed by video from the camp by the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, and invokes the Fifth Amendment, declining to answer the questions put to her. Ten years earlier, under oath in a civil case, her answer had been that she did not recall; now she declines to give an answer at all. Both are lawful. Both are on the record. She is sixty-four, with eleven years of the sentence still to run. The committee closes the session holding exactly the information it opened with.

stops.name: Federal Prison Camp Bryan, the date set for release
stops.date_confidence: attested as the Bureau of Prisons scheduled release date; a future date, not an event
stops.campa: The Bureau of Prisons publishes a release date, and the atlas ends there, because she is alive and there is nothing else to end at: no tomb, no monument, no memorial, no book. She will be seventy-five. Her father will have been in the ground on the Mount of Olives for forty-six years, in a grave the record cannot fix to within four hundred metres. The last stop on this journey is not a place she reached. It is a line on a form, and it is the only ending the case has.
